note: Fuzzer passes raw input bytes as a CoAP PDU to the parser; the PDU contains a Proxy-Uri option whose value is attacker-controlled.
Parses CoAP options from the input buffer; the Proxy-Uri option (option number 35) is extracted with its value and length.
Validates that the Proxy-Uri option length is between 1 and 1034 bytes; the option value is stored in the PDU's option buffer.
After successful PDU parsing, the fuzzer calls coap_get_uri_path which looks for the Proxy-Uri option.
Retrieves the Proxy-Uri option value pointer and length, then passes them to coap_split_proxy_uri for URI parsing.
Forwards the Proxy-Uri option value and length to coap_split_uri_sub with the proxy check flag enabled.
Sets p to the start of the Proxy-Uri value; the buffer is heap-allocated by the PDU parser.
Reads the first byte of the Proxy-Uri value; this is in-bounds since the option length is at least 1.
Attempts to match the 'coap' scheme prefix; if the input is shorter than 'coap', len reaches 0 while q still points into the static scheme string.

code: len = keep_len; p = str_var; q = (const uint8_t *)"http";
note: For proxy URIs, resets len and p to the start, then tries to match the 'http' scheme prefix instead.
Matches the 'http' scheme; if the input is exactly 'http' (len=4), the loop consumes all 4 bytes, len becomes 0, and p points one past the end of the input buffer.
Checks if the next character is 's' for https; since len is 0, this is skipped, so the scheme is set to http.
Tries to match the '://' separator; with len=0, the loop body never executes, and q still points to ':' in the static string.
Since *q is ':' (non-zero), the function returns -2 without reaching the vulnerable path; this input does not trigger the overflow.
For a different input where the Proxy-Uri value is 'http://' followed by a host and path, parsing proceeds past the scheme.
Matches the '://' separator, consuming 3 bytes; p now points to the host portion of the URI.
Sets q to the start of the host; if the host starts with '[', it is treated as an IPv6 address reference.
Scans for the closing ']' in the IPv6 address; if the input is 'http://[abc' (no closing bracket), len reaches 0 and q points one past the end of the buffer.

code: if (!len || *q != ']' || p == q) { res = -3; goto error; }
note: Detects the missing ']' because len is 0, and returns -3 without reading out of bounds.
For input 'http://[abc]' (with closing bracket), the loop stops when *q == ']' with len > 0; q points to the ']' character.
Stores the IPv6 host and advances q past the ']'; q now points to the byte after ']' and len is decremented.
Checks for a port separator; if the byte after ']' is ':', the port parsing begins.
Parses the port digits; if the port is empty (immediately followed by '/'), p == q and no port is set.
At the path label, if len > 0, reads *q to check for a path separator; q is in-bounds when len > 0.
Parses the path component; if the path is non-empty, the path string is stored in the URI structure.
Parses the query string; the remaining bytes are stored as the query.

Returns 0 if all input was consumed; otherwise returns -1. The vulnerable read occurs when the input ends with a partial IPv6 address or malformed host that causes q to advance past the buffer while len is still non-zero due to size_t underflow.

VULNERABILITY: If the input is 'http://[abc]' followed by additional bytes, and the closing ']' is at the very end of the buffer, then after ++q and --len, len becomes 0 and q points one past the end. The subsequent path parsing reads *q when len is 0 due to the check 'if (!len) goto end;' being bypassed by a size_t underflow in the port parsing when the byte after ']' is ':'.
If the byte after ']' is ':' and len was 1, then --len underflows to SIZE_MAX (since len is size_t), causing subsequent reads of *q to be out of bounds.
With len underflowed to SIZE_MAX, the loop reads *q repeatedly past the end of the heap buffer, causing the heap-buffer-overflow READ 1.
